judged_text: The service now performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a credential DB write on every SalesforceCalendarService construction — previously the jsforce connection refreshed lazily — and this new flow never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, so it is disconnected from the credential-sync feature the PR claims to implement. Every Salesforce availability check and booking now makes a synchronous login.salesforce.com round-trip and a DB write even when the stored access token is valid, adding latency to the booking hot path and multiplying token-endpoint load; the change is also implementation work not traceable to any stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor now immediately does a token refresh via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then performs `prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. This refresh/write is unconditional in the shown code path (no check of existing token validity/expiry). Also, unlike other integrations in this PR, it does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (it only uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse`), so it bypasses the credential-sync routing introduced elsewhere. The broader claim that this happens on every availability check/booking depends on when/where this service is instantiated (not shown in the diff), so the impact is an architecture/performance concern rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.
